In [[mathematics]], specifically [[Group theory#Finite group theory|finite group theory]], the '''Gorenstein–Harada theorem''', [[mathematical proof|proved]] by [[Daniel Gorenstein]] and [[Koichiro Harada]], classifies the [[finite simple group]]s of sectional 2-rank at most 4.<ref>{{cite book | last1=Gorenstein | first1=D. | author1-link=Daniel Gorenstein | last2=Harada | first2=Koichiro | author2-link=Koichiro Harada | editor1-last=Gagen | editor1-first=Terrence | editor2-last=Hale | editor2-first=Mark P. Jr. | editor3-last=Shult | editor3-first=Ernest E. | title=Finite groups '72. Proceedings of the Gainesville Conference on Finite Groups, March 23-24, 1972  | publisher=North-Holland | location=Amsterdam | series= North-Holland Math. Studies | isbn=978-0-444-10451-9 |mr=0352243 | year=1973 | volume=7 | chapter=Finite groups of sectional 2-rank at most 4 | pages=57–67}}</ref><ref>{{cite book | last1=Gorenstein | first1=D. | last2=Harada | first2=Koichiro | title=Finite groups whose 2-subgroups are generated by at most 4 elements | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=CzUZAQAAIAAJ | publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]] | location=Providence, R.I. | series=Memoirs of the American Mathematical Society | isbn=978-0-8218-1847-3 |mr=0367048 | year=1974 | volume=147}}</ref> It is part of the [[classification of finite simple groups]].<ref name="Oliver2016">{{cite book|author=Bob Oliver|title=Reduced Fusion Systems over 2-Groups of Sectional Rank at Most 4 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=zDl4CwAAQBAJ&pg=PA3|date=25 January 2016|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]] |isbn=978-1-4704-1548-8 |pages=1, 3}}</ref>

Finite simple groups of section 2 with rank at least 5 have [[Sylow 2-subgroup]]s with a self-centralizing [[normal subgroup]] of rank at least 3, which implies that they have to be of either [[component type]] or of [[characteristic 2 type]]. Therefore, the Gorenstein–Harada theorem splits the problem of classifying finite simple groups into these two sub-cases.
